# Scene Representation and Partitioning

Also called: Spatial decomposition, Scene partitioning, Distributed NeRF training

## Overview
This family encompasses methods that decompose a 3D scene into multiple sub-regions or distinct neural fields to address scalability, dynamic content, or [distributed training](#6233-optimization-and-parallelization.md) constraints. Unlike the canonical single-network [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md), these methods partition the scene representation to enable parallel processing, handle large-scale environments, or separate static and dynamic elements. Key distinctions include MegaNeRF's use of spatial Voronoi cells for data parallelism in large-scale training [8581-meganerf], [NeRFPlayer](#9440-nerfplayer.md)'s [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) into stationary, deformation, and radiance fields for dynamic streaming [9440-nerfplayer], and the distributed spatial partitioning method's use of geometry-based PDFs for balanced GPU workload distribution [10332-spatial-partitioning-for-distributed-nerf].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family build on [Scene Representation and Architecture](11368-scene-representation-and-architecture.md). They retain the core volumetric rendering integral:
$$
C(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i} T_i \left( 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i) \right) \mathbf{c}_i
$$
where $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$ [S1, Parent]. The primary deviation lies in how $\sigma_i$ and $\mathbf{c}_i$ are computed. Instead of a single global MLP, the scene is represented by a collection of local MLPs, fields, or partitions. The rendering process must aggregate contributions from these partitions, ensuring global transmittance $T$ is accumulated correctly across partition boundaries.

## Subtopics

### [MegaNeRF](8581-meganerf.md)
A framework for large-scale scenes (e.g., aerial footage) that partitions the volume into spatial Voronoi cells, each with an independent NeRF submodule. It uses foreground/background decomposition and geometric clustering to enable data-parallel training, addressing the infeasibility of training a single massive network.

### [NeRFPlayer](9440-nerfplayer.md)
A dynamic scene representation that decomposes the volume into a stationary field, a deformation field, and a radiance field. It explicitly models the transition between static and dynamic states, allowing for efficient streaming and high-fidelity reconstruction of dynamic scenes without per-frame multi-view observations.

### [Spatial Partitioning for Distributed NeRF](10332-spatial-partitioning-for-distributed-nerf.md)
A method for distributed NeRF training that partitions the 3D volume into non-overlapping tiles based on a Probability Density Function (PDF) derived from scene geometry. It recursively splits the volume to minimize aspect ratio deviation, ensuring balanced spatial content density across GPUs, unlike camera-location-based partitioning.

## Background
The canonical NeRF [S1, unofficial] uses a single MLP, which scales poorly in memory and compute for large scenes or dynamic content. MegaNeRF [S1, S5] introduced spatial partitioning specifically for scalable training of thousands of images, where pre-training a single network is infeasible. NeRFPlayer [S1] addressed the lack of efficient dynamic scene streaming by separating static and dynamic components. The distributed spatial partitioning method [S1] emerged to solve workload imbalance in multi-GPU training, moving beyond camera-centric partitioning to geometry-centric partitioning.
